In Vega-Lite, the 'temporal' type is used for continuous time data, such as dates and timestamps. When you use 'temporal' for a year column, Vega-Lite will treat the values as dates and will scale the axis accordingly, taking into account the actual time intervals between the values.

On the other hand, the 'ordinal' type is used for categorical data, where the values are treated as distinct categories rather than continuous values. When you use 'ordinal' for a year column, Vega-Lite will treat the years as separate categories, spacing them equally apart on the axis, regardless of the actual time intervals between them.

For a year column, 'ordinal' might be a good choice if you're dealing with annual data where the exact date isn't important, and you want to emphasize the categorical nature of the data. However, if you're working with time-series data where the continuity of time is important, 'temporal' is usually a better fit.

In your case, since you're working with a time-series chart and the 'Year' field represents a continuous timeline, 'temporal' is a suitable choice. However, if you wanted to emphasize the annual nature of the data and didn't care about the exact timing, 'ordinal' could also work.
